Sessions / Session 03 Scene 04 Five Days

Session 03 — At Sea — Five Days

DM Note

Run day by day. Roll d20 flavour, resolve downtime, move on. Day 2 has a hard-scripted beat. Calveno closes Day 5.

Opening

Read Aloud

The storm breaks by mid-morning. The sea settles into long grey swells — nothing like last night. Old Faas has lashed the sail. Thunk is bailing. The ship is moving again, slower than she should be, but moving. Five days to Calveno. What do you do?

Downtime Pitch

Say once at the start of Day 1:

“Eight hours of sleep, eight hours of ship work. That leaves eight hours a day that are yours — five periods total.

Sem‘s at the hull if you want to help with repair or learn from him. Old Faas can teach the charts. The Chart Archive in the captain’s cabin is open. If someone needs real rest, Alys has the surgeon’s berth — three days clears most conditions. The crew is here if you want to know them. Casters: if you want something in your pocket before Calveno, talk to me about scrolls. Otherwise — tell me what your character would actually do with five days at sea.”

Day 2 — The Whale (Perrin)

DM Note

Script this beat on Day 2 regardless of the flavour roll — cut to it after the roll. If Perrin isn’t on watch, call him up:

“Black-Jaw. Come look at this.” The whale is still visible when he arrives.

Read Aloud

No wind, no chop, no roll. The sea has settled flat. The early light is grey. Your breath mists.

Perception — First sighting

DC 10 calm/clear · DC 14 flat water/pre-dawn · DC 18 low visibility. Fail: notices nothing — creature already past; only Perrin sees the last glow. Near miss: bow wave as it’s passing. “There’s a bow wave ahead — and it didn’t come from us.” Success: bow wave, then the creature visible. Bioluminescence, slow exhale column. Crit success: full view from first movement — outline, glow, long breath.

Nature — What is it?

DC 12 species recognition · DC 16 full identification. Fail: calls it a sea monster. Near miss: breathing cycle marks it non-predatory. Nothing more. Success: real species. Bioluminescence and size confirm it. Crit success (DC 16+): same species as the thing in Perrin’s Auralis dream. Give Perrin advantage — if he hits DC 16, he recognises the shape he was inside.

Ask Perrin: does he say anything? Does he tell whoever’s on watch what he knows?

DM Note

Same species as the Auralis dream. Perrin knows that shape — he hunted one from inside. Nobody else has a name for it. The seed: he was inside something that hunts this. He is very small.

Spotlight: Perrin. Secondary: whoever is on watch.

Flavour Table — d20

Roll once per day. Describe to the table before downtime.

d20Central Strait — What they see
1A school of flying fish erupts ahead of the bow — hundreds of silver bodies arcing for thirty seconds, then gone.
2Merchant traffic on the horizon all morning — sails heading west, then east, then west again. The Strait is busy here.
3The water turns pale and milky for two miles — off-white. They lean over and find it: jellyfish, thousands, translucent blue-white, just beneath the surface.
4The water changes colour for an hour — deeper blue-green, noticeably colder. Old Faas calls it a current tongue running up from the Maw. He doesn’t elaborate.
5A pair of Crown frigates heading east in formation. They’re moving fast. Noor watches them through the glass until they’re gone.
6A pod of dolphins rides the bow wave for the better part of an hour.
7A Tessarine merchant brig passes close to starboard, heavy-laden and low in the water. Trade goods moving toward the Crown Islands.
8The sky at dusk goes amber-green. Old Faas says it means calm for two more days, in a tone that suggests calm is not always good.
9A sea turtle surfaces close to the hull — huge, barnacled, indifferent. Old Faas says they’ve been sailing these routes since before the Dravosi built their first pier.
10A mat of kelp the size of the ship drifts north, moving against the surface current. Deep current running the other way, Old Faas says.
11A pair of aarakocra pass high overhead, moving south in a straight line. Courier flight — someone needs word of something fast.
12Bioluminescent plankton in the night wake. The ship leaves a river of cold blue light for three hours. A hand in the water glows.
13A Grung fishing raft passes half a mile to port, net out, catch looking good. Normal as anything.
14Wind dies completely for four hours. Becalmed. Then it returns from a different direction entirely.
15Seabirds by the thousands, resting on the water in every direction. They sail through them for an hour.
16In the early morning, very far away: something large exhaling. Not the ship, not the crew. Old Faas doesn’t look up from his charts.
17A Rattkin trader — small, quick, riding high — cuts across the bow, flying no faction pennant. Normal east of Midchain.
18Stars unusually clear. Noor names most of them and says Tail navigators use completely different names for the same sky.
19Two-hour rain squall with no wind. Flat sea, fifty-foot visibility. The crew works in silence. Then it clears as if nothing happened.
20A whale — a different species from Day 2 — surfaces off the port quarter. Breathes three times and slides under. Old Faas watches it go with an expression no one can read.

Activities

Recover — Alys

  • Condition / disease / poison: DC 15 Con save, advantage with Alys present. Success clears it.
  • Exhaustion: 3 full days removes 1 level. No roll.

DM Note

Grigori as a research source: Answers without hesitation. Accurate and detailed — he has met half the ruling families of the Shattered Sea. For every two questions he answers, he asks one back. He is genuinely curious.

Time with Crew

CrewWhat they’ll talk aboutWhat surfaces

DM Note

Grigori crew time: One of three tells per scene — never sleeps, hands always cold, prays at 3am in a language that isn’t Common. See Shepherd Grigori for full notes.

Day 5 Close

Read Aloud

The fifth morning. The sea has changed — warmer, greener. Old Faas points off the starboard bow without a word. On the horizon: a smear of colour that isn’t water. Calveno.

→ Scene 5 — Calveno Approach.
